cues.en: This is Outperforming Imperative with Pure Functional Languages. I'm Richard Feldman. So for the past couple of years, I've been working on building a programming language called Rock. And Rock is inspired by and a direct descendant of my... What has been my favorite programming language for several years now, which is Elm.
cues.zh: 这是用纯函数式语言超越命令式语言。我是 Richard Feldman。过去几年，我一直在开发一种叫 Rock 的编程语言。Rock 的灵感来自——并且是我的……多年来我最喜欢的编程语言 Elm 的直接后裔。

cues.en: Elm is... One of the things that I love about it is it's it's got this really delightful user experience. It really gives me joy to program in it. It's a pure functional language and it's compiled to JavaScript, so it's really good for making browser based UIs.
cues.zh: Elm……我喜欢它的一点是，它的用户体验非常令人愉悦。用它编程真的让我感到快乐。它是一种纯函数式语言，编译成 JavaScript，所以非常适合做基于浏览器的 UI。

cues.en: But I've wanted sort of like an Elm like experience in other domains besides browser based UIs, and so Rock has similar goals to Elm of having like a delightful user experience, and it's a pure functional programming language like Elm, but it's compiled to binary. So it's sort of for other use cases that that Elm is not meant for at the moment.
cues.zh: 但我一直希望在基于浏览器的 UI 之外的其他领域，也能有类似 Elm 的体验，所以 Rock 有着和 Elm 类似的目标：令人愉悦的用户体验，而且和 Elm 一样是纯函数式编程语言，但它编译成二进制。所以它面向的是 Elm 目前并不适用的其他场景。

cues.en: So I first got into Elm based on this blog post, Blazing Fast HTML and Elm, came out in 2014.
cues.zh: 我最初接触 Elm 是因为这篇博客文章《Blazing Fast HTML and Elm》，它发表于 2014 年。

cues.en: And one of the things that I appreciated about Elm was I had a relatively performance sensitive UI that I was building, and I really like to see this benchmark that sort of gave me confidence that I was gonna have a fast experience when I was building my apps in Elm, and I wasn't gonna a nice experience building it and then have things run slowly when I got done.
cues.zh: 我欣赏 Elm 的一点是，我当时在做一个对性能比较敏感的 UI，我很喜欢看到这个基准测试，它让我有信心：用 Elm 构建应用时会有快速的体验，而不会在构建时体验很好、做完之后却运行缓慢。

cues.en: So I wanna sort of keep that value in rock. Like, it's really important to me that, like, hey, let's go fast. Let's let's build a programming language that runs programs really fast.
cues.zh: 所以我想把这个值保留在 Rock 里面。就像，对我来说这真的很重要，比如说，嘿，我们冲吧。让我们来构建一个能让程序跑得极快的编程语言。

cues.en: Of course, trouble with that is that this is a pure functional programming language, and pure functional programming languages are all about pure functions, as in like every function is pure, and that means no side effects and no mutation, which can be a bit of a challenge when it comes to performance if you're trying to go really fast because
cues.zh: 当然，这带来的麻烦在于，这是一门纯函数式编程语言，而纯函数式编程语言的核心就是纯函数，也就是说每个函数都是纯的，这意味着没有副作用，也没有状态突变。如果你想追求极致的速度，这在性能方面可能会带来一些挑战，因为

cues.en: the fact of the matter is, some algorithms just require in place mutation to run fast.
cues.zh: 事实就是，有些算法天生就需要原地修改（mutation）才能跑得快。

cues.en: Like, for example, how competitive could a pure functional language possibly be at a mutation heavy algorithm like QuickSort?
cues.zh: 比如说，对于像快速排序（QuickSort）这种高度依赖状态突变的算法，一门纯函数式语言到底能有多大竞争力？

cues.en: This seems like somewhat of an intractable, unavoidable downside.
cues.zh: 这看起来像是一个有点难以解决、无法回避的缺点。

cues.en: So fortunately though, are several different considerations to performance, like for example, the language overhead, like how much overhead does the language introduce, sort of how close can it get you to what the hardware is capable of, and that can be sort of balanced against, you know, there's no side effects, there's no mutation. So when you put all those things together, how well can we come out when compared to imperative languages?
cues.zh: 不过幸运的是，关于性能还有几个不同的考量维度，比如语言开销，也就是语言本身引入了多少开销，以及它能在多大程度上接近硬件的极限性能，这些可以与“没有副作用、没有状态突变”这一特点相权衡。所以把所有这些因素综合起来，和命令式语言相比，我们的表现究竟能有多好？

cues.en: Well, let's let's kind of look through these and just talk through them. So first, I'm to talk about language overhead, like in general and also as it pertains to Rock.
cues.zh: 好吧，让我们大致梳理并讨论一下这些问题。首先，我要谈谈语言开销，包括总体上的开销，以及它与 Rock 的关系。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: Haskell is a very well known, probably the most well known pure functional programming language,
cues.zh: Haskell 是非常知名、可能是最知名的纯函数式编程语言，

cues.en: and we actually use it at work where I work at Norite Inc. So our back end for many years was Ruby on Rails, which is a pretty common tech stack, and then in recent years, we've actually been migrating our our our back end from Ruby to Haskell. And so in particular, we migrated one of our services, actually our most high traffic performance critical service to Haskell. This is serving billions of questions every year. We we make software for English teachers, so students are answering billions of questions on our site all going through this Haskell service.
cues.zh: 而我们在 Norite Inc 的工作中确实用它。我们后端的多年技术栈是 Ruby on Rails，这很常见，近年我们一直在把后端从 Ruby 迁移到 Haskell。尤其我们把其中一个服务——实际上是我们流量最高、性能最关键的服务——迁移到了 Haskell。它每年处理数十亿道题。我们为英语教师开发软件，所以学生在我们网站上回答的数十亿道题都要经过这个 Haskell 服务。

cues.en: And what we found was that when we migrated this from Ruby on Rails to Haskell and service, basically doing the same job as it was doing before, slightly different but not really that meaningful from a performance perspective,
cues.zh: 我们发现，把这项服务从 Ruby on Rails 迁移到 Haskell 后，它基本做和以前一样的工作，略有不同，但从性能角度看意义不大，

cues.en: the delta was was quite large in terms of performance. It was about 10 x faster.
cues.zh: 性能差距相当大，大约快了 10 倍。

cues.en: Now this, we're well aware, was not because, like, pure functional programming is like, oh, that... That's... It's this magic sauce that just makes everything run faster.
cues.zh: 我们很清楚，这并不是因为纯函数式编程是让一切跑得更快的神奇配方。

cues.en: No. It definitely wasn't that. It's just because some...
cues.zh: 不，绝对不是。只是因为某些……

cues.en: Imperative versus pure functional, but they just sort of dominated in this case, which led to Haskell being a lot more performance in practice than Ruby was.
cues.zh: 命令式与纯函数式的差异，但在这个场景里它们恰好占了主导，导致 Haskell 在实践中比 Ruby 性能好得多。

cues.en: So let's talk about that execution model a little bit. I mentioned that Ruby's interpreted. There's quite a few languages that will do interpret it basically like interpreting the source code into... Parsing it into an AST and then interpreting that on the fly. So Python, Ruby, JavaScript all do this. May or may not have JIT, which is a just in time compilation, which can speed that up in, like, really tight loops, things like that.
cues.zh: 所以，我们来稍微聊聊这个执行模型。我刚才提到 Ruby 是解释型语言。有不少语言基本上都是通过解释来执行的：先把源代码解析成 AST，然后即时解释执行。Python、Ruby 和 JavaScript 都是这样做的。它们可能会有 JIT，也就是即时编译，可以在非常紧密的循环之类的场景中显著提速。

cues.en: Some languages do interpretive byte codes, so, like, Java, c sharp, Elixir compiling
cues.zh: 有些语言会解释执行字节码，比如 Java、C#，以及 Elixir 编译

cues.en: to Beam byte code.
cues.zh: 生成的 Beam 字节码。

cues.en: Other languages go straight to a binary, like a a... Just an individual stand alone binary. So Go does this, Swift does this, Haskell also does this.
cues.zh: 还有一些语言会直接生成二进制文件，也就是一个独立的可执行二进制文件。Go、Swift 和 Haskell 都是这样做的。

cues.en: These are generally the fastest category of things, like these are pretty much sorted from sort of highest overhead to least overhead,
cues.zh: 通常来说，这类语言的速度最快。大体上，它们是按照开销从高到低排列的。

cues.en: But there's something that's worth calling out as almost a different category onto its own, which is LLVM compiled to binary. So LLVM is basically a library that's for optimizing
cues.zh: 不过，还有一种值得单独指出的，几乎可以算作独立类别的方式，那就是使用 LLVM 编译成二进制文件。LLVM 基本上是一个用于优化

cues.en: compiled binaries.
cues.zh: 编译后生成的二进制文件的库。

cues.en: It's not like LLVM is, like, the only way to get this this extra speed bump, but languages like c plus plus and Rust and Zig all use this to get, like, really, really exceptionally great performance out of their binaries.
cues.zh: LLVM 并不是获得额外性能提升的唯一方式，但 C++、Rust 和 Zig 这类语言都会利用它，让生成的二进制文件获得极其出色的性能。

cues.en: And, of course, that's what we want for Rock two, so that's what we've been using.
cues.zh: 当然，这正是我们希望 Rock two 达到的效果，所以我们一直采用这种方式。

cues.en: I mentioned boxing. So boxing, basically referring to things being allocated on the heap, which generally is a lot slower than allocating them on the stack or in registers.
cues.zh: 我提到了装箱。所以装箱，基本上是指在堆上分配对象，这通常比在栈上或寄存器中分配要慢得多。

cues.en: Some things that can be boxed include numbers. So, like, in Python, numbers are boxed, for example. That means that doing number stuff in Python is generally a lot slower and why you have libraries like NumPy and stuff to to speed that back up.
cues.zh: 可能会被装箱的东西包括数字。所以，比如在 Python 中，数字就是被装箱的。这意味着在 Python 中处理数字通常要慢得多，这也是为什么你需要像 NumPy 这样的库来重新提速。

cues.en: Objects and records also very commonly boxed depending on the language. Functions and closures also potentially boxed depending on the language.
cues.zh: 根据语言的不同，对象和记录也非常常见会被装箱。函数和闭包根据语言的不同也可能被装箱。

cues.en: Basically,
cues.zh: 基本上，

cues.en: you know, that... That's just sort of another source of potential slowness.
cues.zh: 你知道，那……那只是另一种可能导致变慢的原因。

cues.en: Memory management, lots of different memory management strategies. A really common one is sort the old school way. It was like individual allocations and deallocations,
cues.zh: 内存管理，有许多不同的内存管理策略。一个非常常见的策略是老派的方式。也就是单独的分配和释放，

cues.en: like c, c plus plus, Rust, and Zig. These languages will help you out with this. They're not gonna make you do it by hand like you had to in c, like every single allocation,
cues.zh: 比如 C、C++、Rust 和 Zig。这些语言会在这方面帮你一把。它们不会像你在 C 语言中那样让你手动去做，比如每一次分配，

cues.en: specifically call malloc and then call free again.
cues.zh: 都要显式调用 malloc，然后再调用 free。

cues.en: But at the end of the day, like, that is how the memory is being managed. It's sort of like one allocation at a time.
cues.zh: 但归根结底，这就是内存被管理的方式。有点像一次只分配一个。

cues.en: Then you also have tracing garbage collectors, which is a very, very popular strategy these days. So like Go, JavaScript,
cues.zh: 然后你还有追踪式垃圾回收器，这是当今非常非常流行的策略。比如 Go、JavaScript，

cues.en: also like Java, and the list goes on and on for tracing GCs.
cues.zh: 还有 Java，使用追踪式 GC 的语言还有很多很多。

cues.en: Big downside of tracing garbage collector just compared to individual allocations and deallocations is that you get garbage collection pauses. So this is all something that that we're probably familiar with. You know, the program just locks up for for some period of time while it's doing this garbage collection.
cues.zh: 相比于单独的分配和释放，追踪式垃圾回收器的一个大缺点是会产生垃圾回收暂停。所以这可能大家都很熟悉。你知道，程序在进行垃圾回收时会卡顿一段时间。

cues.en: There's another memory management strategy that does not have garbage collection pauses, which is quite nice, which is automatic reference counting. So Python, Swift, and Rock all do this, and the usual downside there is just that the reference counting sort of has more overall overhead typically, so that sort of the throughput is less compared to tracing garbage collector even though you don't have the GC pauses.
cues.zh: 还有另一种没有垃圾回收暂停的内存管理策略，这非常棒，那就是自动引用计数。Python、Swift 和 Rock 都采用了这种做法，而它通常的缺点在于，引用计数整体上会有更多开销，因此与追踪式垃圾回收器相比，吞吐量相对较低，尽管你不会遇到 GC 暂停。

cues.en: One of the things that you can do to sort of reduce that downside and make it so that it it has higher throughput without reintroducing GC pauses is what's known as static reference counting. I know that Swift does this in some form, but I'm not a Swift programmer, not sure exactly how it works. But I know that what we did in Rock to to do this was there were these two papers that we implemented. One is called counting immutable beans. The other is called Perseus.
cues.zh: 为了减少这种缺点并提高吞吐量，同时又不会重新引入 GC 暂停，你可以采取的一种方法就是所谓的静态引用计数。我知道 Swift 在某种程度上也做了这个，但我不是 Swift 程序员，不太确定它的具体工作原理。不过我知道我们在 Rock 中实现这一点时，参考并实现了两篇论文。一篇叫 counting immutable beans。另一篇叫 Perseus。

cues.en: And basically, are two ways of, among other things, optimizing it so that you don't need to do as many reference checks at runtime or as many reference count operations at runtime because we're able to sort of detect at compile time where they would be happening and cancel each other out, we can just kind of throw them away.
cues.zh: 基本上，这两种方法（以及其他优化方式）的作用在于，优化后你就不需要在运行时进行那么多的引用检查或引用计数操作了，因为我们能够在编译时检测到这些操作将要发生的位置并将其相互抵消，从而直接把它们省去。

cues.en: One other thing I wanna note, I don't have time to get all the way into it for this talk, but there's another thing that Rock does that's pretty novel in terms of memory management. The upshot of it is that instead of using automatic reference counting, you can completely transparently to the application author, in some situations,
cues.zh: 还有一点我想提一下，这次演讲我没时间深入讲，但 Rock 在内存管理方面还有另一个相当新颖的做法。简单来说，它没有使用自动引用计数，而是可以在某些情况下对应用开发者完全透明地

cues.en: do arena allocation, bump allocation, which are just way faster than any of these other strategies, including tracing GC, including even individual allocations and deallocations.
cues.zh: 进行 arena 分配、bump 分配，这些方式比其他任何策略都快得多，包括 tracing GC，甚至包括单独的分配和释放。

cues.en: I gave a whole talk about this, so if you're if you're curious about that, you can you can check it out later. But suffice it to say, this is one of the things that I think is going to be most promising for Rock's long term memory management, even though for the rest of this talk, I'm not going to be using it.
cues.zh: 我做过一个完整的演讲专门讲这个，所以如果你好奇的话，可以之后去看看。但简而言之，我认为这是 Rock 长期内存管理中最有前途的方向之一，尽管在这次演讲的剩余部分里我不会用到它。

cues.en: Okay. So to sum up, when it comes to language overhead, we've basically tried to do as good of a job as we can of minimizing the language overhead of Rock. So we're using LLVM. That's, like, basically, it's sort of the gold standard for high performance compiling to binaries
cues.zh: 好。总结一下，在语言开销方面，我们基本上已经尽了最大努力来最小化 Rock 的语言开销。所以我们用的是 LLVM。这基本上算是高性能编译到二进制文件的金标准

cues.en: today.
cues.zh: 了。

cues.en: We're using unboxed values basically everywhere we possibly can. There aren't any values that I know of that are boxed unnecessarily.
cues.zh: 我们尽可能在所有地方使用非装箱值。据我所知，没有任何值是不必要地被装箱的。

cues.en: And when it comes to memory management, we're doing static reference counting along with some more exotic stuff like arena allocation behind the scenes.
cues.zh: 而在内存管理方面，我们采用的是静态引用计数，再加上一些更奇特的东西，比如背后的 arena 分配。

cues.en: So overall, I'm like feeling pretty good about this. Like, okay, I I think we're doing a good job here.
cues.zh: 所以总的来说，我感觉这挺不错的。我觉得，好吧，我觉得我们这里做得挺好。

cues.en: Good start, but that's... That was sort of the upside section. Right? Now we have these two things we have to deal with, which is we're not allowed to do side effects, we're not allowed to do mutation,
cues.zh: 开局不错，但那是……那算是积极的一面。对吧？现在我们必须处理这两件事，也就是我们不能有副作用，我们不能做变异操作，

cues.en: so how do we compete when those are our restrictions? So let's talk about the no side effects thing. Well, fortunately, of the two, this one turns out to not be as big of a deal as you might guess.
cues.zh: 那么在有这些限制的情况下我们该如何竞争？所以我们来谈谈没有副作用这件事。嗯，幸运的是，在这两件事中，这一件并没有你想象的那么严重。

cues.en: A common question that I hear asked of of people who talk about pure functional programming languages is, are you just heating the CPU up?
cues.zh: 我经常听到有人问那些谈论纯函数式编程语言的人一个问题：你们是在白白加热 CPU 吗？

cues.en: Side effects are like everything. So, I mean, like, what what are you doing?
cues.zh: 副作用就像是一切。所以，我的意思是，你们到底在干什么？

cues.en: Haskell doesn't do side effects, is most of our production traffic running on Haskell? Is it just, not doing any effects? Is it never talking to database? No. Of course not. It's doing all those effects. They're just not side effects. Still effects, but they are now managed effects.
cues.zh: Haskell 没有副作用，难道我们大部分的生产流量都在 Haskell 上运行吗？难道它真的不做任何副作用操作？它从来不跟数据库交互吗？不。当然不是。它在做所有这些副作用。只是它们不再是副作用了。依然是副作用，但它们现在是受控副作用。

cues.en: So side effects versus managed effects, that's really the trade off we're talking about here when it comes to performance.
cues.zh: 所以副作用与受控副作用，这才是我们在性能方面真正讨论的权衡。

cues.en: So here's an example of something that does side effects. This is JavaScript doing... Using Promises. So we're setting promise one equals fetch some URL. Promise two is fetch the URL dot then, and then there's some callback which is gonna return another promise. You could chain these together, etcetera, etcetera.
cues.zh: 所以这是一个产生副作用的例子。这是 JavaScript 在做……使用 Promise。所以我们设置 promise one 等于 fetch 某个 URL。Promise two 是 fetch 那个 URL 点 then，然后会有一个回调函数来返回另一个 Promise。你可以把这些链式串联起来，等等，等等。

cues.en: Promises are a super common thing in JavaScript. They're nice for modeling asynchronous tasks that that can sort of be chained together,
cues.zh: Promise 在 JavaScript 里是非常常见的东西。它们非常适合用来对那些可以串联起来的异步任务进行建模，

cues.en: and it's something that is done all over the imperative world. Managed effects, now hold on because this is gonna look extremely different.
cues.zh: 而且这在命令式编程世界里到处都在用。托管副作用，大家先别急，因为接下来这个看起来会非常不一样。

cues.en: As you can see, this is super different and and weird and alien.
cues.zh: 如你所见，这真的非常不同、很怪异，甚至有点生疏。

cues.en: No. It's the same thing. It's basically just promises. The only the only difference is, like, this is a Elm syntax, so it's a little bit different. Instead of a dot then, you have a pipe to and then, but same basic thing. So if you ever look at a, like, large pure functional program, structurally, it's very, very similar to promises.
cues.zh: 不。其实是一回事。它基本上就是 Promise。唯一的区别在于，这是 Elm 语法，所以稍微有点不同。不用 `.then`，而是用管道符 `to` 然后接着写，但基本原理是一样的。所以如果你看过那种大型的纯函数式程序，从结构上讲，它跟 Promise 非常非常相似。

cues.en: The only difference is that with promises,
cues.zh: 唯一的区别在于，对于 Promise 来说，

cues.en: right when you instantiate the promise, it runs the effect. Like, as soon as you call fetch, boom. It does the HTTP request right then and there. Whereas with managed effects, it's basically... You're building up the same structure, but it doesn't get executed right away. Instead, you build up this big sort of chain together task, you hand that off to main, and then the the language runtime will actually execute that when you start the program.
cues.zh: 就在你实例化 Promise 的那一刻，副作用就开始运行了。比如，只要你调用 fetch，砰！HTTP 请求当下就发出了。而对于托管副作用来说，基本上……你构建的结构是一样的，但它不会立即执行。相反，你会构建出这种大型的串联任务，把它交给 main 函数，然后语言运行时会在你启动程序时实际执行它。

cues.en: That's the only difference. So it's nothing mysterious. It doesn't feel like a a totally different, you know, way of doing effects. It's just like kinda like Promises, but you do that everywhere. Now one important difference when it comes to performance is that you do have to do this for all effects.
